proposals.before: Do you think I would cast away my generals because of mere subordinates?"
proposals.after: Do you think I would cling to my generalship?”
proposals.reason: Chinese 豈以臣重去將哉 asks whether Chen Yu begrudges abandoning the generalship (去將), not discarding subordinate generals; 」 closes his speech here.

proposals.before: Would you imagine I would discard my generals over mere subordinates?"
proposals.after: Would I take abandoning the generalship as a weighty matter?”
proposals.reason: Literal English mirrors the same misreading of 去將 as discarding generals rather than leaving the general's office; 」 closes the speech.

proposals.before: "The general said he wanted only the Zhao king."
proposals.after: The general said, "You want only the king."
proposals.reason: Chinese 若欲得王耳 is the Yan general's answer about what the visitor wants; the idiomatic line wrongly wraps narrative attribution in quotes and reverses the referent of 若.

decisions.reason: 豈以臣重去將哉 asks whether Chen Yu would regard abandoning the generalship (去將) as weighty; the corrected reading retains the closing quotation mark required by 」 and the preceding speech.
The same 去將 means leaving the general's office, not discarding generals; the corrected literal retains the closing quotation mark required by 」.
燕將曰：「若欲得王耳」 has the general addressing the visitor (若 = you) about wanting only the king; the original misquotes narrative attribution and makes the general the one who wants the Zhao king.
